data.summary: `ddflow gate status` prints a recorded SuiteBusy unavailable reason in the present tense ("blocked on pid 989929 ... you are #2 in the queue") with no timestamp, long after the wait ended, so it reads as a live queue entry. The suite lock itself is healthy, nothing on disk is stale. The fix is in the display: show when the outcome was recorded and that it is a past timeout, and say the gate only needs re-running. The trailing NOTE "ci, unit_tests did not run" adds to it: ci has a recorded partial run with 1651 passed.

data.summary: The expired-lease refusal says "To take it over: ddflow recover --item X, then ddflow claim X --force", and help topic recovery says "Either way the item is taken back with ddflow claim <item> --force". But api/lifecycle/claim.py claim() does `force = force and not _agent_marker_of(agent)`, so an agent's --force is dropped without saying so and the only agent route is --approval. The ddflow_claim `force` parameter text adds a third story: "only to retry after ddflow_recover said a crashed agent's tree holds nothing", which contradicts the help for a tree that holds work. An agent reading the refusal is told to retry a flag that cannot work, and each retry can count toward [approvals].auto_approve_after_retries. Found by reading the code on PS-snapshot-calibrate 2026-11-05; --force was not run. The refusal should give an agent only the route that applies to it, and the three texts should agree.
data.title: Expired-lease claim refusal and recovery help send an agent to --force, which claim drops for agents
